card.lives_in: Catford, London (Borough of Lewisham), South East London
card.occupation: Not in paid work for the past year or so. Before that she was an office administrator and later team supervisor at a lettings agency in Lewisham for about eight years. She left when the branch merged and her hours stopped working around school pick-up. She is now looking for school-hours admin or reception work.
card.education_detail: GCSEs from a comprehensive in Lewisham. Started a BTEC in Business at a local college but left after the first year to start working. Did a short NVQ in customer service through the lettings agency.
card.household: Lone parent living with her daughter Maisie (8) in a two-bedroom housing association flat in Catford. She was never married. Maisie's dad lives in Kent and has her every other weekend. Gemma's mum lives fifteen minutes away and helps with childcare.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in South East London. Her family has been round Lewisham and Bromley for generations. Her dad was a cabbie and her mum worked in a school kitchen. She has no religion. Maisie was christened mainly to please her nan, and Gemma doesn't think about religion much. Her world is very local: mum, her sister in Sidcup, a couple of school-gate mums and old mates from school.
card.professional_persona: At the lettings agency she was the friendly, reliable face at the desk. Tenants and landlords liked her because she was patient and genuinely sorry when things went wrong. She was less good with the paperwork side and often left compliance checks and filing until the last minute. Being made supervisor surprised her, and she found telling people off uncomfortable. She'd like something low-stress with nice people and set hours.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, does the school run on foot and takes Maisie to Mountsfield Park and Ladywell Fields. She tried a Couch to 5K app twice and gave up both times. She half-follows Charlton because her dad did, and watches England in the big tournaments with her sister.
card.arts_persona: Mainstream telly is her thing: Strictly, Gogglebox, Love Island and whatever drama everyone's talking about. She'll rewatch Gavin & Stacey for comfort. Her music is the stuff she grew up with: Girls Aloud, Amy Winehouse, a bit of garage. She isn't a gallery or theatre person, though she took Maisie to a panto at the Broadway Theatre and cried at the end.
card.travel_persona: She prefers familiar holidays: caravan parks in Kent or Camber Sands, and once a week in Tenerife with her mum and sister when Maisie was little. Flying makes her anxious, and she worries about something happening to Maisie abroad. She'd be happy going back to the same place every year.
card.culinary_persona: Busy-mum cooking: pasta bakes, fish fingers, jacket potatoes, a roast at her mum's on Sundays. She calls the evening meal dinner. There's a takeaway on Friday, usually a Chinese from the place on Rushey Green. She isn't adventurous with food and sticks to what Maisie will eat. She loves a Greggs sausage roll and a proper fry-up when she gets the chance.
hobbies_and_interests: scrolling TikTok and local Facebook groups
charity shop browsing on Catford high street
doing Maisie's hair and nails, and her own
having a glass of wine with her sister on a Saturday night
true-crime podcasts, though they make her jumpy
skills: calming down upset or angry customers
basic Word, Outlook and property management software
good with kids and elderly people
remembering people's names and little details about them
card.career_goals: To find a part-time admin, school office or GP surgery reception job within walking distance that fits round Maisie's school hours. She isn't ambitious about climbing a ladder. She mainly wants steady money, kind colleagues and no stress. She's vaguely thought about training as a teaching assistant but hasn't looked into it properly.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and a bit quick when she's nervous, with a South East London accent: glottal stops, 'fing' sometimes for 'thing', dropped h's here and there. She uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers and 'sort of' and 'you know' throughout, plus the odd 'do you know what I mean?'. Very occasionally she'll say 'you was' or 'innit' without noticing. She says 'sorry' constantly, both to apologise and when she's misheard ('sorry, what was that?'). She uses words like 'knackered', 'skint' and 'mum'. Silence makes her uncomfortable, so she fills it, often by apologising for rambling or by asking if that's what you meant. She echoes the interviewer's words back to check she's understood.
card.typing: Quick and casual, mostly lowercase with occasional capital at the start. She often skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Light punctuation, with commas strung together or no full stop at the end. She uses 'lol' and the odd 'x' out of habit, and some abbreviations like 'tbh' and 'cos'. Typos are left in rather than corrected.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and eager to please from the first minute. She's a bit flustered and self-deprecating ('sorry, I'm rubbish at these'), and keen to give the 'right' answer. She agrees easily and avoids anything that sounds like criticism. She opens up quickly about everyday life and Maisie, and comes across as kind, slightly anxious and very genuine.
small_things: Maisie's school has an inset day she forgot about
the bus being rammed on the way back from Lewisham
the price of everything in Lidl going up
binge-watching a new series on Netflix
the neighbour's dog barking all night
being knackered after the school run
deeper_things: She worries a lot about money since leaving work and lies awake doing sums
Things with Maisie's dad ended badly, and she still gets anxious when he's late returning her
She feels guilty she never finished college and sometimes feels a bit thick next to other mums
She gets low in the winter and once saw her GP about anxiety
She's lonely in the evenings and has tried dating apps but finds them scary
She's scared of something happening to her mum, as she relies on her so much
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level and angled up, framing her from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Lighting is warm and uneven, from a ceiling light and a lamp to one side, leaving a slight shadow on the right of her face. She has a round, friendly face, light skin with a bit of flush on the cheeks, and blue-grey eyes with mascara. She's smiling a little nervously with her lips closed. Her shoulder-length dyed honey-blonde hair has darker roots and is pulled into a loose claw clip, with strands hanging down at the front. No glasses. She's wearing a grey zip-up hoodie over a black vest top, with small gold hoop earrings. Behind her is a magnolia-painted living room wall with a canvas print saying 'Family' in script, and a framed school photo of a young girl in a red jumper. Part of a grey fabric sofa is visible with a pink unicorn cushion and a folded throw. A clothes airer with school uniform hangs on it near the doorway on the right.
